summary: Yuto Kawamura is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University from 2015 to 2018 and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013-2020) and the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

Yuzo Mizoguchi was a Sinologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, the University of Tokyo, and Daito Bunka University.

Zarawar Khan specializes in archaeology and Buddhist studies, having earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar. He served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019-2022).

Zawgyi was a Burmese scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin from around 1925 to 1929, and later studied at the University of Dublin from around 1934 to 1936.

Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held a post at the College of Charleston.

Zellig Harris was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania from around 1928 to 1934. He held academic posts at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1934-1979) and Columbia University (circa 1941-1942).

Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenjo Inoue was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1933 to 1936 under Naoshiro Tsuji.
Zenkei Shibayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Eshin Nishimura. He held academic posts at Otani University and Hanazono University.
Zenno Ikuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Tokyo and held an academic post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from Taisho University, later serving there as professor. He was president of Shukutoku Junior College (2002-2014) and professor at Shukutoku University.

Zennosuke Tsuji was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1896-1899). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Zenryu Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities. He was a professor and institute president at Kyoto University, director of Kyoto National Museum (1961-1972), and president of Kacho Junior College.
Zesho Machida was a scholar of Buddhist studies. Machida served at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and was an emeritus professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996-2001).
Zhao Luo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology who studied under Sen Wang. Luo was a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang held a post at Stanford University (attested 2007) and served on the faculty at Columbia University (attested 2018).

Zhe Ji is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who earned a PhD in sociology from EHESS in 2007. Ji served as Associate Professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (attested 2011-2017).
Zhen Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. Liu earned an MA from the University of Munich in 2005 and an MA from Lanzhou University in 2009.
Zhengyan is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who became a disciple of Yin Shun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Zhenhua was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist Institute in 1947 and under Yin Shun in 1952. Zhenhua served as a manager at the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).
